title: What the Market Was For
summaryZh: 十一個攤商決定一起試一個辦法。第四個星期三,一個穿西裝的人走進市場,所有人都以為麻煩來了。

sentences.text: It took Nadia two weeks to talk to the other ten sellers.
sentences.zh: 娜迪雅花了兩個星期,跟其他十個攤商談過一輪。

sentences.text: She did not take the notebook with her, because she knew what was written in it.
sentences.zh: 她沒有把筆記本帶在身上,因為裡面寫什麼她都記得。

sentences.text: The plan was small enough that nobody could really argue with it.
sentences.zh: 那個計畫小到沒有人真的能反對。

sentences.text: Each seller would bring one thing that was not theirs to sell.
sentences.zh: 每個攤商都多帶一樣不屬於自己本行的東西。

sentences.text: Milk at the egg stall. Soap beside the potatoes. Bread next to the flowers.
sentences.zh: 蛋攤上放牛奶。馬鈴薯旁邊放肥皂。花攤旁邊放麵包。

sentences.text: The list came from what eighty-six people had told her they bought elsewhere.
sentences.zh: 這張清單來自八十六個人告訴她、他們在別的地方買了什麼。

sentences.text: There was no sign, no name for it, and no announcement of any kind.
sentences.zh: 沒有招牌,沒有取名字,也沒有任何宣傳。

sentences.text: Two of the sellers said it would not work and joined anyway.
sentences.zh: 有兩個攤商說這不會有用,但還是加入了。

sentences.text: The oldest of them said only that his father had done the same thing in 1974.
sentences.zh: 年紀最大的那位只說,他父親一九七四年也做過一樣的事。

sentences.text: Nobody wrote anything down, and nobody asked what would happen if it failed.
sentences.zh: 沒有人寫下任何東西,也沒有人問萬一失敗了怎麼辦。

sentences.text: On the first Wednesday, eleven new customers came.
sentences.zh: 第一個星期三,來了十一位新客人。

sentences.text: Karim counted them from the end of the aisle and wrote the number on his hand.
sentences.zh: 卡林站在走道尾端數,把數字寫在手上。

sentences.text: Eleven was not enough to save anything, and everybody there knew it.
sentences.zh: 十一個救不了什麼,在場每個人都心知肚明。

sentences.text: "Give it a month," Nadia said, to the sellers and to herself.
sentences.zh: 「再給一個月,」娜迪雅說,說給攤商聽,也說給自己聽。

sentences.text: The second Wednesday brought nineteen, and the third brought twenty-four.
sentences.zh: 第二個星期三來了十九個,第三個星期三來了二十四個。

sentences.text: It was growing, but slowly, the way a small thing grows.
sentences.zh: 確實在成長,但很慢,像小東西那樣慢慢長。

sentences.text: Nadia started standing at the entrance for the first hour of every market.
sentences.zh: 娜迪雅開始在每次市場的頭一個小時站在入口。

sentences.text: She was not selling anything at the entrance. She was saying people's names.
sentences.zh: 她在入口不賣任何東西。她在叫人的名字。

sentences.text: Good morning, Mrs. Haddad. Good morning, Mr. Sarr. Good morning, Ines.
sentences.zh: 早安,哈達太太。早安,薩爾先生。早安,伊內絲。

sentences.text: Karim thought it was strange for about two weeks, and then he stopped thinking so.
sentences.zh: 卡林覺得這件事很奇怪,大概持續了兩個星期,之後就不覺得了。

sentences.text: On the fourth Wednesday a man in a grey suit walked into the market.
sentences.zh: 第四個星期三,一個穿灰色西裝的男人走進市場。

sentences.text: Nobody in the aisle had ever seen him before, but everybody guessed who he was.
sentences.zh: 走道上沒有人見過他,但每個人都猜得到他是誰。

sentences.text: The sellers went quiet in the way people do when they expect trouble.
sentences.zh: 攤商們安靜了下來,那是人們預期麻煩上門時的那種安靜。

sentences.text: He introduced himself as Mr. Diallo, the manager of the supermarket on the ring road.
sentences.zh: 他自我介紹叫迪亞洛先生,是環城路上那間超市的店長。

sentences.text: Then he said something nobody in the market had prepared an answer for.
sentences.zh: 接著他說了一句話,市場裡沒有人準備好要怎麼回。

sentences.text: "My mother had stopped leaving her flat," he said. "For nearly a year."
sentences.zh: 「我母親本來已經不出門了,」他說。「將近一年。」

sentences.text: "Somebody told her about Wednesday. Now she comes here and she talks to people."
sentences.zh: 「有人跟她說了星期三的事。現在她會來這裡,而且會跟人講話。」

sentences.text: "I sell her everything she needs and I could not sell her that."
sentences.zh: 「她需要的東西我都賣,但那樣東西我賣不了。」

sentences.text: He asked whether the market would use his car park on Saturday mornings.
sentences.zh: 他問,星期六早上市場願不願意用他的停車場。

sentences.text: The market was so quiet that Nadia could hear the flags moving above the stalls.
sentences.zh: 市場安靜到娜迪雅可以聽見攤位上方旗子飄動的聲音。

sentences.text: Nadia said that she would have to ask the other ten sellers first.
sentences.zh: 娜迪雅說她得先問過另外十位攤商。

sentences.text: She asked them that same afternoon, and by evening the answer was yes.
sentences.zh: 她當天下午就問了,到了傍晚,答案是好。

sentences.text: The market is still eleven stalls, and the empty half is still empty.
sentences.zh: 市場還是十一個攤位,空掉的那半邊還是空的。

sentences.text: Nadia still does not know whether she will get through the coming winter.
sentences.zh: 娜迪雅還是不知道自己能不能撐過即將到來的冬天。

sentences.text: What she knows is what the market was always for, underneath the vegetables.
sentences.zh: 她知道的是,在蔬菜底下,這個市場一直以來真正的用處是什麼。

sentences.text: You can buy an onion almost anywhere in this town, and it will cost you rather less.
sentences.zh: 在這個鎮上,幾乎哪裡都買得到洋蔥,而且便宜得多。

sentences.text: But on a Wednesday morning, somebody in that aisle says your name twice.
sentences.zh: 但在星期三早上,那條走道上會有人叫你的名字兩次。

questions.q: What did the eleven sellers agree to do?
options: Each would stock one item outside their own trade
Each would lower prices to match the supermarket
Each would open on Saturday as well as Wednesday

questions.q: Why did Mr. Diallo come to the market?
options: Because the market gave his mother something he could not sell her
Because he wanted the sellers to close down for good
Because he had been asked to buy their vegetables

questions.q: How does the story leave Nadia's situation?
options: Still uncertain, but clear about what the market is for
Fully solved, with the empty stalls filled again
Worse than before, with the sellers about to give up
